family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a filename and a string of individually invalid characters, remove every character from the filename that appears anywhere in invalid_chars, keeping the relative order of the remaining characters.
hidden_tests: assert strip_invalid_chars('no bad chars', '') == 'no bad chars'
assert strip_invalid_chars('remove all vowels', 'aeiou') == 'rmv ll vwls'
assert strip_invalid_chars('nothing to remove', 'qzx') == 'nothing to remove'
reference:
def strip_invalid_chars(name, invalid_chars):
    return "".join(c for c in name if c not in invalid_chars)

spec: Replace every occurrence of the reserved Windows filename characters < > : " / \ | ? * with an underscore, then strip any trailing spaces or period characters from the end of the resulting name.
hidden_tests: assert sanitize_filename_windows('no bad chars here.txt') == 'no bad chars here.txt'

spec: Replace every run of two or more consecutive underscore characters in the filename with a single underscore, then strip any leading or trailing underscores from the result.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: If a filename ends with the same non-empty extension repeated twice in a row, separated by periods (for example 'file.tar.tar'), remove one of the two duplicate trailing extensions so it appears only once (giving 'file.tar'). If the filename does not end this way, return it unchanged.

spec: Build a filename slug from the given name: lowercase it, replace every run of one or more non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen, and strip any leading or trailing hyphens. Then truncate the result to at most max_len characters, and if that truncation leaves a trailing hyphen, strip it too.
hidden_tests: assert safe_slug_filename('Very Long File Name That Needs Truncation', 10) == 'very-long'
